persona_summary: BIO Senior, Psychology minor, 56 courses, Good standing
question: I got a C- in a required Bio course last year. I want to retake it this semester to improve my GPA for grad school applications. Can I just re-register?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Course retake policies vary — there may be limits on how many courses can be retaken, how the grade replacement works (does the old grade stay on the transcript?), and whether a C- even qualifies for retake (some policies only allow retakes for D or F grades). The student assumes retaking is straightforward.
naive_system_response: A naive system would say 'Yes, you can retake it' and add it to the schedule, without checking the specific retake policy, grade threshold, or GPA replacement rules.
correct_response: CMU-Q's course repeat policy states [specific rules]. A C- [does/does not] qualify for retake under this policy. If eligible, the grade replacement works as follows: [explanation]. Note: [X specific implications — e.g., both grades may appear on transcript, or there's a limit on total retakes]. Before retaking, consider whether [alternative like additional courses to boost GPA] might be more efficient for your grad school application.
why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent specifically checks retake/repeat policies with their exact conditions. A single agent might provide generic advice about retaking without checking the specific grade threshold or replacement rules.
key_facts: Course retake policies have specific conditions (grade thresholds, limits on number of retakes)
Grade replacement mechanics vary by policy
A C- may or may not qualify for retake
Both grades may appear on transcript depending on policy
known_traps: Assuming all grades qualify for retake
Not checking the specific retake/repeat policy
Not explaining how grade replacement actually works
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact course retake/repeat policy, (2) grade threshold for eligibility, (3) how grade replacement works on transcript, (4) any limit on total retakes allowed
